sub: Named after “kneeling” (jāthiyah): every nation on its knees, ayah 28
theme: Allah’s signs are everywhere, yet the arrogant mock them and deny the Hereafter. The surah proves the Day is coming, when every nation kneels before its record and justice is done.
story: Revealed in Makkah, reportedly right after Ad-Dukhān. The two surahs are so alike they read like twins. Most say all of it came before the migration; some place ayah 14 in Madinah.

Makkah’s disbelievers heard the Quran and turned away in pride, mocking its verses. They denied any life after death: “we just live and die, and time wears us out.” Then they dared the Prophet ﷺ: “Bring our dead fathers back.”

The surah answers with signs in the universe and in themselves, the lesson of the Children of Israel, and the Day every nation kneels before its record. Meanwhile the believers are told to forgive and leave the repayment to Allah.

sections.title: Signs fill the universe; woe to the arrogant liar who mocks them
sections.meaning: The Book comes from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise. The heavens and earth, your own creation, animals, night and day, rain and winds are all signs. If people reject these, what will they believe? Woe to the sinful liar who hears the verses, stays arrogant and mocks them. Hell awaits him. The Quran is guidance.
points: Ḥā Mīm: the Book is sent down from Allah, Mighty and Wise
Signs in the heavens, yourselves, animals, night and day, rain, winds
After Allah and His verses, what will they believe?
Woe to the sinful liar who hears, persists proudly and mocks
Hell ahead, no help from wealth or idols; the Quran is guidance
sections.matters: It sets out the two responses to Allah’s signs: people of faith who learn from them, and the arrogant who hear them and walk away as if deaf. It also warns early that mocking the verses ends in Hell.
sections.story: The sinful liar of ayah 7 is reportedly an-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith. Other reports name al-Ḥārith ibn Kaladah, or Abū Jahl and his friends. The word “every” makes it about anyone who behaves like them.
explained: Ḥā Mīm. This Book is sent down from Allah, al-ʿAzīz al-Ḥakīm. Then look around: the heavens and earth, your own creation from a drop, creatures spread everywhere, night following day, rain that brings dead land back to life, winds turning every way. The endings climb step by step: signs for believers, for people of certainty, for people who reason.

If they reject Allah’s own verses, what speech will they ever accept? Woe to every affāk athīm, a liar in word and sinner in deed. He hears the verses, then carries on proudly as if deaf, and jokes about whatever he learns of them. Hell lies ahead; wealth and idols won’t help. This Quran is guidance.
teaches: Creation is full of signs; stop and reflect on them.
Use your mind: the signs speak to people who reason.
Pride can make a person act as if he never heard.
Never turn the Quran into a joke.
Wealth and false protectors are useless before Allah.
sections.hook: Ayat 3–5 each end with who the signs are for: believers, then people of certainty, then people who reason. Ayah 13 later adds a fourth: people who give thought.

sections.title: Allah subjected sea and sky to you; believers are told to forgive
sections.meaning: Allah made the sea carry your ships so you can trade and be grateful, and made everything in the heavens and earth serve you, all from Him. The believers are told to forgive those who don’t fear Allah’s days; Allah will repay each people. Every deed, good or bad, comes back to its doer.
points: The sea carries ships by His command, so you seek His bounty
Everything in the heavens and earth serves you, all from Him
Tell believers to forgive those who don’t expect Allah’s days
Good is for yourself, evil against yourself; then back to your Lord
sections.matters: After warning the mockers, the surah turns to blessings: everything around you was put at your service, so be thankful. Then it tells the believers how to treat those who abuse them: forgive, and leave the repayment to Allah.
sections.story: Ayah 14 reportedly came when a Makkan idolater insulted ʿUmar and he wanted to strike him. Other reports place it in Madinah, involving ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy or a Jewish man. It may have been revealed more than once.
explained: Allah tamed the sea so ships sail by His command, carrying trade and goods from far lands, so that you give thanks. He made everything in the heavens and earth serve you: sun, moon, stars, mountains, rivers, animals and plants. Jamīʿan minhu: all of it is from Him alone. People who think see the signs.

Then a command: tell the believers to forgive those who don’t hope for ayyām Allāh, His days of reward and punishment. Bear their harm; Allah Himself will repay every people for what they earned. Whoever does good gains from it, whoever does evil loses by it, and everyone returns to their Lord.
teaches: Everything that serves you is a gift from Allah; thank Him.
Earning a living is seeking Allah’s bounty.
Don’t take revenge for every insult; leave the repayment to Allah.
Your good and your evil both come back to you.
sections.hook: The section opens at the ۞ mark on page 499 with sakhkhara, “subjected,” twice: the sea (12), then everything in the heavens and earth (13). Ayah 14 opens page 500.

sections.title: Children of Israel got the Book but split; follow your clear path
sections.meaning: Allah gave the Children of Israel the Scripture, judgement, prophethood and good provision, and preferred them over others. They had clear proofs, yet split out of envy after knowledge came. Now the Prophet ﷺ is on a clear way: follow it, not the desires of those who don’t know. Allah protects the God-fearing.
points: Scripture, judgement, prophethood, good things; preferred above the worlds
They split only after knowledge came, out of envy
Follow your sharīʿah, not their desires; Allah backs the God-fearing
The Quran: insight for people, guidance and mercy for the certain
sections.matters: The blessing Israel lost, a revealed Book, has now come to this ummah, with a warning not to repeat their split. It also comforts the Prophet ﷺ: they rejected the truth out of envy, not for lack of proof.
sections.story: No specific incident for 16–17. Ayah 18 reportedly came when Quraysh urged the Prophet ﷺ to return to his forefathers’ religion, saying they were better than him.
explained: Allah gave the Children of Israel the Torah, the wisdom to judge by it, prophets, pure food like manna and quails, and preferred them over the people of their time. He gave them clear proofs. Yet they split, not from ignorance but after knowledge came, out of baghy: envy and rivalry. Allah will judge between them.

Then We put you on a sharīʿah, a clear way. Follow it, not the desires of those who don’t know. They can’t protect you from Allah at all. Wrongdoers are allies of one another, but Allah is the ally of the muttaqīn. This Quran is baṣāʾir, clear insight for people, and guidance and mercy for those with certainty.
teaches: Envy can split people even after the truth is clear.
Follow the revealed way, not people’s desires.
Allah is the protector of those who fear Him.
Carrying the Book is an honour and a responsibility.
sections.hook: Section 1 closed with hādhā hudā, “this is guidance” (11). This section closes the same way: hādhā baṣāʾir… wa hudā (20). Ayah 18 pairs “follow it” with “don’t follow their desires.”

sections.title: Evildoers won’t equal believers; deniers follow desire and say time destroys us
sections.meaning: Will evildoers be treated like believers? Creation is in truth, so every soul gets what it earned. The one who made desire his god has his hearing, heart and sight sealed. Deniers say only time destroys us and demand their fathers back. Allah gives life and death, then gathers all.
points: Evildoers equal to believers in life and death? An evil judgement
Created in truth, so every soul is repaid, none wronged
He took his desire as his god: ears, heart, eyes sealed
“Only this life; only time destroys us”: pure guesswork
“Bring back our fathers!” Allah gives life, death, then gathers you
sections.matters: It gives the surah’s main arguments for the Hereafter: justice demands it, since the good and the wicked can’t end up the same. It also exposes the root of denial: following desire, then calling guesswork knowledge.
sections.story: Ayah 21 reportedly answered Makkan idolaters who told the believers: “If you’re right, we’ll be better off than you in the Hereafter too.” Ayah 23 is linked to Abū Jahl, who privately admitted the Prophet ﷺ was truthful yet refused to follow him.
explained: Do those who pile up sins think they’ll be treated like believers who do good, alike in life and death? What an evil judgement. Allah created the heavens and earth bil-ḥaqq, with purpose and justice, so every soul is repaid for what it earned. Tamīm ad-Dārī reportedly spent a whole night in prayer repeating ayah 21.

Then there is the one who made his hawā, his desire, his god, doing whatever he fancies. Allah left him astray and sealed his ears, heart and eyes. Such people say only ad-dahr, time, destroys us. That is a guess. Their proof? “Bring back our fathers.” But Allah gives life, then death, then gathers everyone on the Day.
teaches: Good and evil can never end the same; justice needs a Hereafter.
Obeying desire over Allah is a kind of worship.
Don’t call guesses knowledge.
Don’t curse time; Allah runs the nights and days.
The One who gave you life can bring you back.
sections.hook: The deniers say namūtu wa naḥyā, “we die and we live” (24). The reply flips the order: Allah gives you life, then death, then gathers you (26). Ayah 23 opens page 501.

sections.title: The Hour: people of falsehood lose, every nation kneels before its record
sections.meaning: Allah owns the heavens and earth. The Day the Hour comes, the people of falsehood lose everything. Every nation will be on its knees, called to its book: “Today you are repaid for what you did. This record of Ours speaks the truth about you; We had everything you did written down.”
points: Allah owns heavens and earth; at the Hour the falsifiers lose
Every nation kneeling, called to its record: today you are repaid
Our record speaks the truth; We had all your deeds written
sections.matters: This is the scene that names the surah: whole nations on their knees. After the deniers’ guesses in the last section, here is the reality they doubted, with a record that misses nothing.
sections.story: No specific incident. It answers the deniers of the previous section by showing the Day itself.
explained: All the dominion of the heavens and earth belongs to Allah. On the Day the Hour comes, al-mubṭilūn, those who built their lives on falsehood, will be the losers, and everything they relied on disappears. You will see every nation jāthiyah: on its knees in fear, waiting for judgement.

Every nation is called to its kitāb: its record of deeds, or, in another view, the law its prophet brought. They are told: today you are repaid for what you did. This record of Ours speaks against you with truth. Nastansikh: We had your deeds written down, nothing added and nothing left out.
teaches: What you rely on besides the truth will vanish on that Day.
Every deed is being recorded.
Live now as someone whose record will be read out.
sections.hook: The surah’s name is in ayah 28: jāthiyah. Kull ummah, “every nation,” comes twice in that ayah, and ayat 28 and 29 both end mā kuntum taʿmalūn, “what you used to do.”

sections.title: Believers enter mercy; mockers forgotten in the Fire; all praise is Allah’s
sections.meaning: Believers who did good enter their Lord’s mercy: the clear success. Deniers are rebuked: the verses were recited, you were arrogant, and you said you only guessed about the Hour. Today they are forgotten as they forgot this Day, with no helper and no way out. All praise and grandeur belong to Allah.
points: Believers who did good enter His mercy: the clear success
Deniers rebuked for pride and doubt; what they mocked surrounds them
Forgotten as they forgot; no exit, no chance to make amends
Praise to the Lord of heavens, earth, worlds; His is the grandeur
sections.matters: The records now decide two ends. Every excuse of the deniers, pride, mockery and guesswork, comes back to face them. The surah then closes by returning all praise and greatness to Allah, the Mighty, the Wise, just as it opened.
sections.story: No specific incident. It completes the scene of the Day for both groups, the believers and the deniers.
explained: Those who believed and did good enter their Lord’s raḥmah, His mercy, which is Paradise: al-fawz al-mubīn, the clear success. The deniers are rebuked: weren’t My verses recited to you? You were too proud. Told the Hour was certain, you said, “We only guess.” Now their evil deeds show, and the punishment they mocked closes in.

“Today We forget you, as you forgot the meeting of this Day.” They are left in the Fire with no helper, because they mocked Allah’s verses and this world fooled them. No way out, and no chance to make amends. So all praise is Allah’s, Lord of heavens, earth and all the worlds, and His is al-kibriyāʾ, all grandeur.
teaches: Faith with good deeds is the real, clear success.
Repayment matches the deed: forgetting Allah is met with being forgotten.
Don’t let this world fool you into forgetting the meeting.
Accepting the truth counts now, not after seeing the Day.
All greatness belongs to Allah alone.
sections.hook: Ayah 36 repeats rabb three times: heavens, earth, all the worlds. Ayah 37 ends with al-ʿAzīz al-Ḥakīm, just as ayah 2 did. It is also the last ayah of Juz 25.

groups.text: Ḥā Mīm. This Book is sent down from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise.
The heavens and earth, your creation, animals, night and day, rain and winds are signs for believers, the certain and those who reason.
These are Allah’s verses, recited in truth. After them, what will they believe?
Woe to the sinful liar who hears the verses, stays proud as if deaf, and mocks them.
Hell is ahead; wealth and idols won’t help. The Quran is guidance, and its rejecters get a painful punishment.
Allah made the sea carry your ships and made everything in the heavens and earth serve you, all from Him.
Believers should forgive those who don’t fear Allah’s days. Every deed returns to its doer, and all return to Allah.
The Children of Israel got the Book, prophethood and favour, but split out of envy after knowledge came.
You are on a clear way: follow it, not the desires of those who don’t know. Allah protects the God-fearing.
This Quran is insight for people, and guidance and mercy for those with certainty.
Evildoers won’t be treated like believers. Creation is in truth, so every soul gets what it earned.
The one who made his desire his god: Allah sealed his ears and heart and veiled his eyes.
Deniers say there is only this life and time destroys us, but that is only a guess.
They demand their fathers back. Allah gives life and death, then gathers all for the Day beyond doubt.
Allah owns the heavens and earth; when the Hour comes, the people of falsehood lose.
Every nation kneels, called to its record, which speaks the truth about everything they did.
Believers who did good enter Allah’s mercy: the clear success.
Deniers are rebuked for pride and for doubting the Hour; their deeds appear and what they mocked surrounds them.
Forgotten as they forgot this Day, they stay in the Fire for mocking the verses, with no way out.
All praise and all grandeur belong to Allah, Lord of the heavens, the earth and the worlds, the Mighty, the Wise.

1.explain: Ḥā Mīm: two separate letters. Allah knows best what He means by them, and He revealed nothing without wisdom.

2.explain: Tanzīl al-kitāb: this Quran is sent down from Allah, al-ʿAzīz, Mighty in His rule, and al-Ḥakīm, Wise in what He makes. So honour it and take it seriously.

3.explain: The heavens and earth themselves are signs of Allah’s power and oneness, for the muʾminīn, those who believe.

4.explain: In your own creation, from a drop to a full human, and in every creature He spread out, are signs for people with yaqīn, firm certainty.

5.explain: Night and day taking turns, rain called rizq because it brings provision, dead land revived, winds turning every way: signs for people who reason. The endings climb: belief, certainty, understanding.

6.explain: These are Allah’s verses, recited in truth. If they reject Allah’s own words and proofs, what speech could they ever believe?

7.explain: Wayl: woe, a word of punishment. Affāk: a habitual liar. Athīm: steeped in sin. He lies in his words and sins in his deeds.
7.why: Reportedly about an-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith. Other reports name al-Ḥārith ibn Kaladah, or Abū Jahl and his companions. “Every” makes it cover anyone like them.

8.explain: He hears the verses recited, then yuṣirr: persists, too proud to believe, as if he never heard them. So give him news of a painful punishment.

9.explain: When he learns anything of the verses, he turns it into a joke. For mocking the Quran, his punishment is humiliating.

10.explain: Min warāʾihim: Hell is ahead of them, or, in another view, trailing behind them. Their wealth and the idols they took as protectors won’t help at all.

11.explain: Hādhā hudā: this Quran is guidance out of misguidance. Those who reject their Lord’s verses get rijz: a painful, agonising punishment.

12.explain: Allah tamed the sea so ships sail by His command. You seek His bounty through trade, bringing goods from far lands, so that you give thanks.

13.explain: Sun, moon, stars, rivers, animals, plants: all made to serve you. Jamīʿan minhu: all of it from Him alone, with no partner. Signs for people who think.

14.explain: Tell believers to forgive and bear the harm of those who don’t hope for ayyām Allāh, His days of reward and punishment. Allah will repay them. Some say this was before fighting was permitted; others say it still stands.
14.why: Reportedly a Makkan idolater insulted ʿUmar, who wanted to strike him. Other reports: at Banū al-Muṣṭaliq, ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy said “Fatten your dog and it will eat you,” and ʿUmar took his sword; or a Jewish man in Madinah said Allah was in need.

15.explain: Whoever does good benefits himself; whoever does evil harms only himself. Then all of you return to your Lord, who repays good with good and evil with evil.

16.explain: Allah gave the Children of Israel the Scripture, al-ḥukm (judging by it), prophethood, pure provision like manna and quails, and preferred them over the people of their time.

17.explain: They had clear proofs of the religion. They split only after knowledge came, out of baghy: envy and rivalry among themselves. Allah will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection.

18.explain: Then We put you on a sharīʿah: a clear way of the religion. Follow it, and not the desires of those who don’t know.
18.why: Reportedly revealed when Quraysh urged the Prophet ﷺ to return to his forefathers’ religion, saying they were better than him.

19.explain: If you followed them, they couldn’t protect you from Allah at all. Wrongdoers stand by each other, but Allah is walī al-muttaqīn, the protector of the God-fearing.

20.explain: Baṣāʾir: clear insights, markers people can see by. The Quran is that for all people, and guidance and mercy for those with certainty.

21.explain: Ijtaraḥū: those who earned evil deeds. Do they think they’ll be like the righteous, the same in life and death? Sāʾa mā yaḥkumūn: what a terrible judgement.
21.why: Reportedly some Makkan idolaters told the believers: “If what you say is true, we’ll be better off than you in the Hereafter, just as we are here.” Another report links it to the duel at Badr.

22.explain: Bil-ḥaqq: Allah created the heavens and earth with truth and justice, so every soul is repaid for what it earned. The believer and the disbeliever can’t be equal, and no one is wronged.

23.explain: Have you seen the one who made hawā, his desire, his god? Allah sent him astray ʿalā ʿilm: knowing he deserved it, or after knowledge reached him. His hearing and heart are sealed, his sight veiled.
23.why: Reports differ: al-Ḥārith ibn Qays, one of the mockers; or Abū Jahl, who privately admitted the Prophet ﷺ was truthful but refused to follow him, fearing Quraysh would say he did it for a crust of bread.

24.explain: They say: only this worldly life; some die, others are born, and ad-dahr, time, wears us out. They have no knowledge, only guesses. The Prophet ﷺ taught not to curse time, since Allah runs night and day.
24.why: Reportedly the people of the Jāhiliyyah said that time is what destroys us and gives us life and death, and this ayah was revealed about them.

25.explain: When the clear verses about resurrection are recited, their only argument is: bring our dead fathers back, if you are truthful. They wanted to push the message away, not find the truth.

26.explain: Say: Allah gave you life, then gives you death, then gathers you for the Day of Resurrection, not in this world. Most people don’t know; if they did, they would prepare for it.

27.explain: To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and earth. The Day the Hour comes, al-mubṭilūn, the people of falsehood, lose: everything they built on falsehood collapses.

28.explain: Jāthiyah: kneeling on the knees in awe and fear, waiting for judgement. Every nation is called to its kitāb, its record of deeds, and told: today you are repaid for what you did.

29.explain: This record of Ours speaks against you with truth. Nastansikh: We had the angels write down everything you did, with nothing added or missed.

30.explain: Believers who did good enter their Lord’s raḥmah, His mercy, which is Paradise. That is al-fawz al-mubīn: the clear, obvious success.

31.explain: The disbelievers are rebuked: weren’t My verses recited to you? But you turned away in pride and were a criminal people.

32.explain: When told Allah’s promise is true and the Hour is certain, you said: we don’t know what the Hour is; we only guess, and we are not convinced.

33.explain: The ugly results of what they did become visible, and ḥāqa bihim: the punishment they used to mock closes in on them from every side.

34.explain: Nansākum: today We leave you in the punishment as if forgotten, just as you forgot, and never worked for, the meeting of this Day. The Fire is your home, and no one helps.

35.explain: Because you mocked Allah’s verses and worldly life fooled you. They won’t be brought out, and lā yustaʿtabūn: no one asks them to make amends, since excuses and repentance no longer count.

36.explain: Fa-lillāhi l-ḥamd: all praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the heavens, Lord of the earth, Lord of all the worlds, for keeping His promise and for all He created.

37.explain: Al-kibriyāʾ: all greatness and majesty in the heavens and earth are His, and no one may rival Him in it. He is al-ʿAzīz, never overpowered, al-Ḥakīm, putting everything in its place.
